item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 30 September 2026
item.description:
Tipa turns Frosthaven’s Quatryl Library into tower defense, funneling machines into one lane and setting up a huge Trapper trap detonation.

Frostilyte adds Seadra to his low-tier Pokémon Silver run, mainly because Lance’s Dragonites need another fast Aurora Beam problem.

Sey says TOEM 2 keeps the original’s monochrome charm while adding jumping, tools, puzzles, and more reasons to chase perfect photos.

Azuriel argues Valheim’s real design brilliance is food and base-building, especially how the campfire makes survival feel meaningful without hunger nagging.

Bhagpuss meant to coast through easy-mode Valheim, but raft misery, island-hopping, and dreams of a Plains homestead pulled the adventure back in.

Margot enjoys BloomKeeper’s cute real-time herding, land-reviving Pouics, and the comic joy of yeeting little seed pals across the map.

Shintar drops into WoW Brewfest and comes away delighted by ram racing, the hourly cooking event, and a surprisingly real sausage-eating contest.

Wilhelm hits 310 million skill points on his EVE Online main, then zooms out to a very on-brand 20-year accounting of 436 million total.

Juhis shares two small Home Assistant quality-of-life tweaks, including a self-resetting skip-next-dim toggle for late-night writing or coding.

Mike digs into a corroded Sharp X68000 ACE I/O board, wrestling battery damage, brittle plastics, and a crusty SASI connector.

Dave Winer fixes a subscription bug, praises Don’t Look Up, notes an RSS Chat Go implementation, and riffs on sports, bodies, and inheritance.

Brennan explains his blog’s new black-and-white Moonflower look as part design refresh, part meditation on tradition, ritual, and taking things seriously.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 29 September 2026
item.description:
Stargrace checks in on WoW goldmaking with 3.2 million in sales, pet flipping, token prices, and thoughts about returning to Wyrmrest Accord.

Syp keeps the WoW Forever wait bearable by pre-planning guilds, alts, professions, and a six-character legacy roster.

Magi chats with Skyler Zeng about Sleepover, a cosmic horror visual novel leaning hard into isolation, insignificance, and two girls left on Earth.

Luna has a good time with Magical Blush’s elemental metroidvania combat and Brazilian folklore touches, even if some late-game friction starts to bite.

Emily has a real love-hate ride with Death Stranding, praising its striking porter premise while wrestling with Kojima’s dense lore and marathon cutscenes.

Oya says TOEM 2 nails the same monochrome charm, photo-taking, and cozy questing that made the original such a delight.

Ellie tackles the impossible task of reviewing Marvel vs. Capcom 2, focusing on why Capcom’s tag fighter still towers over the series.

Wilhelm joins an EVE Online Flycatcher swarm for a low-sec brawl, with drag bubbles, friendly bubbling mishaps, and plenty of killmail-chasing chaos.

Tobold weighs buying Transport Fever 3, partly because Steinwallen’s videos and affiliate links make supporting long-form YouTube feel fair and practical.

Anarchae rounds up links on Matrix chat, car surveillance kill switches, battery fires, PWHL on CBC, and a welcome Podcast Addict update.

Joel’s weeknotes juggle pixel art, Switch pickups, bookstore temptation, Le Guin, and a weirdly memorable supermarket blackout.

Bruce Schneier cools the RSA panic: this is an implemented old forgery attack on unpadded signatures, not a private-key recovery breakthrough.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 28 September 2026
item.description:
Roger shares a straightforward workaround for LOTRO’s patch server bug, including launcher flags for both default installs and Steam.

CrazyKinux pulls leadership lessons from an Asher Elias interview, framing EVE Online coalition management as logistics, herding, and player retention.

Shintar is delighted SWTOR’s 8.0 PTS brings back animated character creation hangar backgrounds, restoring some lost environmental storytelling.

Kimimi gushes over Forgotten Realms: Demon Stone as a gloriously kinetic D&D action game with cinematic pacing and smart little tactical flourishes.

Wilhelm rounds up Fantasy Critic week 39, with Control Resonant and Silent Hill: Townfall posting solid scores while Nighthawks still waits on reviews.

The Chronicler spotlights 1920: Nest of Eagles, a Polish-Soviet War hex-and-counter game with friction lines, reaction movement, and a friendlier learning curve.

Bhagpuss follows a recommendation rabbit hole into 2Hollis and The Femcels, sharing a brisk, catchy tour of new music discoveries.

Warner’s Sunday links roam across AI harms, misinformation, simpler living, sports writing, and gambling’s ugly modern shadow.

Ramen Junkie moves the blog from WordPress to Hugo, chasing a leaner Markdown-first workflow, more control, and fewer platform headaches.

Dave Winer reflects on Apple’s missed support for Frontier and celebrates getting the old DocServer building again during the port.

Cristian shares a video on the enduring appeal of the 2012 ThinkPad, that old-school laptop holdout favorite.

Kelly argues blogging isn’t dead, just diminished, with IndieWeb and frustration over social media ownership keeping the personal web alive.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 27 September 2026
item.description:
Stargrace says EverQuest Legends is mostly daily sky grinding, class unlocks, and gear farming right now—more obligation than fun, honestly.

CrazyKinux finished a massive EVE Online asset haul across 153 systems, turning repetitive logistics into a practical crash course in lowsec survival.

Margot’s week mixed sickness, cozy puzzle games, and a surprisingly well-run Xbox Fanfest, even if the Fable demo slots were long gone.

Shintar is excited for WoW Forever, but worries the same social pressures and race-to-keep-up mindset could spoil what she loves about World of Warcraft.

Marc traces how Might & Magic evolved into Clash of Heroes, the Capybara-made DS spinoff that turned tactical RPG ideas into puzzle battles.

Anarchae’s weekly digest covers sickness, job-hunt burnout, and getting hooked on Hyperion and Fall of Hyperion during a rough in-between stretch.

Ramen Junkie’s week was a time-warp of vacation days, work reshuffles, and Transformers hunting, with Target preorder chaos finally easing a bit.

Warner riffs on leadership, groupthink, and Meta’s Muse, arguing human follow-the-leader instincts make the AI moment feel more hive mind than progress.

Wilhelm rounds up recent binge-watching, from another twisty Harlan Coben Netflix mystery to Silo’s AI-heavy bridge season and Lucky on Apple TV.

Cristian shares a simple photo-journal moment: went out for eclairs, came home with more goodies than planned.

Brennan argues programming should treat kindness as intentional infrastructure, pushing back on the culture-war nonsense framing empathy as weakness.

Tipa looks back on Daily Blogroll, arguing AI summaries helped surface indie blogs even as scaling curation and anti-AI backlash sank the project.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 26 September 2026
item.description:
John says Ambrosia Sky is basically Prey meets PowerWash Simulator, with Saturn-ring stations, fungal cleanup, immersive-sim puzzles, and a grappling tether.

Tipa jumps back into Malifaux’s fall league, ditches struggling Colette, and gets another win with Rasputina while eyeing new modes and Gaining Grounds.

Frostilyte recommends 20 More, Somehow Even Smaller, Mazes as a free, breezy antidote to time-sink games, with clever little twists throughout.

Wilhelm wraps Planet Crafter’s free Skeo with a nice appreciation of its dramatic terraforming, unlockable exploration, and loot-heavy icy-to-tropical transformation.

The Friendly Necromancer details the absurd EverQuest Legends faction grind to unlock Trolls, plus a few handy farming tricks and wishlist tweaks.

Tobold wonders whether MMORPG discourse and today’s AI criticism share a deeper link, via names like Ed Zitron and Cory Doctorow.

Roger shares a brisk batch of wise quotes on knowledge, science, change, and cleaning up your own messes.

Bruce Schneier spots a Tennessee family squid dissection event and, naturally, invites readers to go take pictures.

Syp makes a cozy case for tiny single-purpose gadgets, especially an X3 e-reader and iPod Nano combo for distraction-free porch reading.

Jeff Atwood shares a moving Stack Overflow story that argues human help mattered more than any LLM ever could.

Jeff is launching HomelabFest in St. Louis for homelabbers into self-hosting, efficient servers, old hardware, racks, and budget builds.

Joel reflects on a sci-fi movie post that grew into something else, with some fun side-chat about blogging formats and punctuation habits.
